Changelog

ClustAssess 1.3.0 (unreleased)

Algorithm and performance

These are implementation changes, not a measured end-to-end speedup or memory-reduction guarantee. See PERFORMANCE.md in the source repository for tradeoffs and measurement requirements.

  • Reworked flat disjoint ECS partition comparison paths used by merge_partitions() and related consistency scoring.
  • Added compact label-invariant keys for duplicate partition matching, with the same label equivalence as the exact comparison and no numeric-to-text rounding. Exact comparisons guard against hash collisions.
  • Avoided unnecessary pairwise ECS matrix construction when callers only need aggregate ECC values (for example element_consistency() and unordered merging).
  • Reused exact single-cluster-count summary ECC instead of recomputing the same weighted consistency result.
  • Avoided hidden PSOCK dispatch for non-identity ECS-threshold partition merging; that internal path runs serially.
  • Added native C++ batch paths for weighted_element_consistency(), serial element_sim_matrix(), and corrected_l1_mb_at_once() that encode each partition once and execute the exact IEEE-754 arithmetic, pair summation order, compensated mean, element names, and .Random.seed semantics of 1.2.0 (with automatic O(n) sparse handling for high-cardinality pairs—also added to direct pairwise disjointECS() and disjointECSaverage()—and exact R fallback for mixed, classed-weight, bytes-encoded, missing-name, or missing-label cases).
  • Replaced igraph-based binary search and union loops in get_highest_prune_param(), get_highest_prune_param_embedding(), and get_nn_conn_comps() with native C++ disjoint-set operations on CSC / kNN-index arrays for standard dgCMatrix inputs with positive integer n_neigh (falling back to the R implementation otherwise). Standard binary NN inputs with nonzero cutoffs avoid materializing the unpruned SNN matrix (zero-cutoff and weighted inputs still construct the full SNN matrix); inputs with explicit stored zero entries now return a valid pruned matrix instead of failing.
  • Reused each selected configuration’s exact PCA kNN index across get_nn_conn_comps() and assess_nn_stability() inside automatic_stability_assessment() via a scoped cache cleared on exit.
  • Centralized NN/SNN graph construction from precomputed neighbor indices. PCA graph stability now builds one neighborhood’s graph matrices at a time in the main process rather than building all neighborhoods in parallel on workers.
  • Changed final clustering-stability and PCA NN-stability scheduling to group jobs into balanced worker chunks (strided across resolutions/seeds in assess_clustering_stability() and contiguous seed chunks in assess_nn_stability()), cutting PSOCK IPC overhead while preserving exact nested results and seed order. All memberships for an algorithm are retained before summarization; progress advances after those jobs finish.
  • Replaced repeated full-library utils::installed.packages() scans in is_package_installed() with find.package(..., quiet = TRUE).
  • Made forced garbage collection in stability workflows opt-in via options(ClustAssess.force_gc = TRUE). Avoiding forced pauses can also delay memory reclamation; normal R garbage collection remains active.
  • Leiden with leidenbase (clustering_algorithm = 6): a worker reuses the igraph and edge weights of the last adjacency matrix it clustered for the next clusterings of the same matrix, rather than building them for each clustering and start. Each worker keeps a copy of that matrix’s data and its igraph.

Results are those of 1.2.0, except for the fixes under “Correctness and robustness” and these implementation effects:

  • merge_partitions() and element_consistency() no longer create R’s random number state (.Random.seed) when none exists while they look for identical partitions with numeric labels; 1.2.0 created it in the native code of that check. They create it only where two partitions without character labels are then compared, as 1.2.0 also did. These functions draw no random numbers.
  • Serial similarity matrices no longer warn that %dopar% runs sequentially, and their errors no longer start with task 1 failed.

API and options

  • Added make_pca_matrix_processing() for explicit exact PCA and optional fixed-seed irlba-backed approximate PCA. The factory uses the input’s rank limits and ambient BLAS settings, whereas the default processor caps components at half the feature count, with a minimum feature-derived cap of one, and controls BLAS threads when RhpcBLASctl is available. Exact factory processing is therefore not necessarily equivalent to the default.
  • Added compute_umap_embeddings to assess_feature_stability() and automatic_stability_assessment() so callers can skip feature UMAP output when only stability scores are required.
  • Added return_nn_idx to assess_nn_stability() and automatic_stability_assessment() to reduce result size when stored neighbor indices are not needed.
  • Added opt-in return_partition_seeds to assess_nn_stability() to expose the existing merged representative’s seed and RNG kinds for each UMAP graph type and neighbor count, without retaining all embeddings or neighbor matrices.

Correctness and robustness

  • Fixed the writing of the app’s expression file (write_objects(), used by write_shiny_app()) for one-gene chunks (both a last block of one gene and chunk_size = 1 when writing rank_matrix) and clamped HDF5 rank_matrix chunk height to min(chunk_size, nrow(expression_matrix)) so small filtered matrices do not trigger chunk-dimension warnings.
  • Fixed SharedObject::unshare() cleanup calls across feature, graph, and clustering stability so the shared object (rather than the unshared input) is unshared, including on worker error paths via on.exit() / tryCatch(..., finally = ...).
  • Fixed four leaked new[] heap buffers and a 32-bit integer overflow in src/wilcox.cpp::wilcox_test() (n1 * (n1 + 1) overflowed for n1 >= 46,341).
  • Added input/index bounds validation in get_highest_prune_param_embedding() and getNNmatrix() so fractional or out-of-range neighbor counts and indices raise R errors instead of aborting R, and rejected non-finite weights in get_highest_prune_param().
  • Fixed parallel_nn2_idx() when more workers are registered than rows in embedding by capping parallel chunks to nrow(embedding).
  • Fixed automatic_stability_assessment() so save_temp = FALSE is respected during the connected-components and NN-stability stages, n_top_configs is capped per feature set rather than carried over across sets, and single-step feature sets no longer fail during incremental ranking.
  • Fixed integer overflow in element_sim() when the cell count times a cluster size exceeds the integer range, which could produce negative, infinite, or inflated similarity values. The optimized similarity-matrix and threshold merging paths also use this corrected calculation.
  • Fixed average ECS for partitions whose numeric label ranges contain unused values.
  • Made flat numeric labels consistent across scalar/per-element ECS, reference comparisons with element_agreement(), ECC, similarity matrices, and partition merging. Fractional, negative, large, and precision-sensitive labels retain their equality pattern instead of being truncated or rounded through integer/text conversion. Internal compact encoding also avoids allocating tables from raw label ranges.
  • Flat membership vectors with missing labels (NA or NaN) now stop with a clear error where 1.2.0 failed on them, often by stopping R in native code. Where 1.2.0 gave a result, the missing labels are compared as 1.2.0 compared them:
    • two vectors of numbers or factors are compared as 1.2.0 compared them in native code: a vector whose labels are all missing is one cluster. A vector with only some missing labels, and any missing label where character labels are compared, stop;
    • merge_partitions() with ecs_thresh = 1, and element_consistency(), merge a list with missing labels first as 1.2.0 merged it: in its order and with its check, also for the partitions without missing labels (character and factor labels through table(), where both have a label and with the unused levels of a factor; other labels as integers). They stop where 1.2.0 failed to compare two of the partitions left. Of these, the partitions without missing labels that give the same partition are then merged, as without missing labels;
    • a comparison with a hierarchical or overlapping clustering puts the element with a missing label in no cluster;
    • merge_partitions() and element_sim_matrix() accept a list of one such partition.
    Vectors of different lengths are not the same partition, which 1.2.0 could find for numbers. Empty-string labels remain valid.
  • Fixed exact duplicate merging for numeric relabellings whose label ranges contain unused values.
  • Fixed the avg_agreement value of merge_partitions() (frequency and agreement ordering): after duplicate or threshold merging, it now uses the frequencies of the merged partitions. Before, it could use the frequencies of the input records, which gave wrong values (for example a low value to a partition found in most repetitions) and a wrong order of tied partitions. Ordering by agreement, and breaking frequency ties by it, can change.
  • merge_partitions() with frequency or agreement ordering now gives avg_agreement 1 when every repetition found the same partition; before, that result had no value. An agreement given with the input is kept, and a single repetition has no value, as before.
  • Fixed exact duplicate merging of factors to ignore unused factor levels.
  • Fixed merge_partitions() to forward return_ecs_matrix and check_ties through pre-merged and nested partition inputs.
  • Fixed merge_partitions(return_ecs_matrix = TRUE) so the full returned ECS matrix follows partition order after frequency tie-breaking.
  • Fixed UMAP argument handling in feature stability, graph stability, and connected-component assessment to honor umap_arguments$n_neighbors instead of silently replacing it with 15. The default remains 15, capped at the cell count minus one. Results can change for previously ignored explicit settings.
  • Fixed UMAP graph-stability handling for custom seed sequences and for repeated neighbor counts, which stopped with an error. A repeated count is assessed once, as in PCA graph stability.
  • Fixed NN-only and SNN-only UMAP graph-stability output names. PCA NN-only graph stability (graph_type = 0) no longer returns extra PCA_snn summaries.
  • Fixed Leiden worker dependency selection in assess_clustering_stability() to use clustering_algorithm rather than the auxiliary arguments list.
  • Fixed Leiden with leidenbase (clustering_algorithm = 6):
    • its results are named Leidenbase; they were stored under NA, which the Shiny app and get_clusters_from_clustassess_object() could not read;
    • it uses Seurat’s partition type, RBConfigurationVertexPartition (modularity with a resolution parameter, on the scale of Louvain), unless clustering_arguments sets partition_type. leidenbase’s own default, the Constant Potts Model, reads the resolution on another scale and put almost every cell in its own cluster at the usual resolutions;
    • assess_feature_stability(), assess_nn_stability() and the matching steps of automatic_stability_assessment() accept it, as assess_clustering_stability() did.
    • with several starts (num_starts above 1 in clustering_arguments), it gives the same partitions for the same seeds. Each start now gets a seed drawn from the clustering’s seed; it had none, so leidenbase seeded it from the clock and the partitions changed from run to run. R’s random number state after the clustering is as before.
  • Fixed assess_feature_stability() with graph_reduction_type = "UMAP", also as a step of automatic_stability_assessment(): each repetition’s UMAP now starts from the seed of that repetition, as in assess_nn_stability(). It started from R’s random number state at that time unless umap_arguments had a seed, so runs on several workers gave other results each time. Results change where umap_arguments had no seed.
  • Fixed the point shapes of plot_k_resolution_corresp(), plot_k_n_partitions() and the Shiny app for five or more clustering methods or configurations: the fifth had no shape, or the plot failed. The shapes repeat after the five filled ones. The app’s method filters show every method by default, Leiden_matrix and Leidenbase included.
  • Fixed the Shiny app’s plot of the number of partitions per number of clusters with its legend at small text sizes, which stopped with “figure margins too large”: its legend row now holds the margins of its plots.
  • Fixed the Shiny app’s plots with a legend (the plot of the number of partitions per number of clusters, the boxplots of the clustering and feature stability, and the UMAPs) at large text or legend sizes or on narrow screens, which stopped with “figure margins too large” when the legend left the plot no room: the legend text is then drawn smaller, or the plot without its legend when even a small one does not fit. A UMAP colour bar at a small legend size, under its UMAP or on its own, which stopped in the same way, now fits. The plots that 1.2.0 drew are drawn as before, whatever graphical parameters the caller set. After par(new = TRUE), the plots with a legend row are drawn as in 1.2.0, as are the separate colour bar and the feature stability plots drawn into one figure of a caller’s own layout of several figures.
  • Fixed automatic_stability_assessment() to record the actual embedding dimension in stable_config$n_pcs, including for custom matrix processors.
  • Unified feature-count normalization between feature and automatic assessment, fixing cache misses for large double-valued counts and fractional counts. Counts below one or above the feature-set size, including infinities, use all features before integer conversion; missing counts are omitted. Cache fallbacks and single-feature processors receive dimension-preserving cells-by-features matrices. Default PCA retains one component for a one-feature subset.
  • Fixed combined PCA/UMAP graph assessment to merge named summaries without corrupting neighbor indices, and to pass clustering arguments to both paths. A UMAP winner now rebuilds the final graph from its evaluated representative seed and worker RNG kinds, including PSOCK RNG streams. Replay restores the caller’s RNG state. The seed is recorded as stable_config$umap_seed, and the graph-building embedding is returned when requested. PCA winners keep PCA neighbor indices.
  • Feature stability and graph stability (PCA and UMAP, also their counts of connected components) now take the results of the repetitions in seed order, whatever order the workers finish in. One core and doParallel gave this order before; with a backend that returns results as they finish, the representative partitions and their order, and the merges at a threshold below 1, no longer depend on worker timing. The feature-stage UMAPs in feature_stability$embedding_list stay unchanged; the umap of a selected configuration can be replaced by the embedding of the winning UMAP graph.
  • Made RhpcBLASctl and SharedObject genuinely optional on default PCA and parallel nearest-neighbor paths. Missing packages leave BLAS settings alone or use ordinary matrix exports; behavior with the packages installed is retained.
  • Exact PCA remains the default. Approximate PCA remains opt-in, uses a fixed seed for deterministic matrix processing, and restores the caller RNG state.

Testing and benchmarks

  • Added correctness and regression coverage for ECS edge cases, PAC scoring, graph construction, matrix processing, automatic stability assessment, final clustering stability, and PSOCK worker paths.
  • Added benchmark and profiling harnesses for ECS, graph construction, matrix processing, automatic stability assessment, and clustering-stability worker scaling.
  • Added a release-branch comparison benchmark harness with optional function tracing, Rprof/Rprofmem output, and saved results (with MD5) for separate parity checks. The harness does not itself compare saved results.
  • Added a Linux process-session RSS/PSS sampler so PSOCK memory comparisons include the main process and all workers.
  • Require testthat 3.2.0 or newer for regression-test binding mocks, and use a supported Matrix coercion in clustering test fixtures.

Documentation

  • Added portable PERFORMANCE.md and analysis/bench/README.md guides with correctness boundaries, runtime/memory tradeoffs, validation commands, and requirements for comparable measurements.
  • Documented downstream UMAP consumers and RNG considerations for stochastic steps when optional feature UMAP computation is disabled.
  • Updated the pipeline and dimensionality-reduction vignettes for explicit UMAP neighbor counts, processor contracts, retained outputs, and actual embedding dimensions. Separate dependency/data setup from rendering, clean up example worker processes, and fix composite QC figure construction.
  • Made real-data benchmark paths explicit caller inputs; excluded raw benchmark artifacts from Git and package builds.

ClustAssess 1.2.0

CRAN release: 2026-08-29

Updates

  • Add subsetting option for the Shiny heatmaps and bubbleplots. The subset is based on already existing metadata columns.
  • Use leidenbase package for Leiden clustering instead of leiden (aligning with Seurat’s changes). Algorithm=6 contains the leidenbase implementation, whereas algorithm=4 and 5 are associated with leiden (for matrix and igraph input objects, respectively).
  • Minimise redundant calculations of the adjacency matrix in the automatic assessment.
  • Add function that calculates the nn2 index in parallel.
  • Add an ordering of the points in the metadata shiny plots based on the order of the input subgroups.
  • Scale the colour values of gene expression in ShinyApp based on provided cap value.
  • Control the number of values shown on the continuous UMAP legend.
  • Add option to download multiple genes in separate UMAP files.
  • Removes ggtext dependency from the package (used in the shiny gene UMAP plots).

Fixes

  • Ensure the expression matrix or embedding has row names. If not, set them to “cell_1”, “cell_2”, etc.
  • Treat the case when enrichment analysis returns no results.
  • Sort the group 2 markers for enrichment analysis based on the absolute logfoldchange.
  • Discard the metadata columns with too many unique values for visualisation in the Shiny app.
  • When creating a Seurat object, the number of PCs is set to the minimum between 30 and half the number of genes. This is to avoid errors when the number of genes is low.

ClustAssess 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2025-05-27

Updates

  • Add barplot with Cell count or percentage of metadata in the Shiny context.
  • Add option to combine (split) metadata and dynamically create a new metadata column in the Shiny context.
  • Add option to calculate the percentage of cells expressing gene above a threshold in the summary table from the Shiny Violin section.
  • Add hierarchical plot that shows the relationship between partitions with different number of clusters.
  • Add the option to create the ClustAssess app without the need to run the stability assessment (the light version). If the clustassess parameter is NULL, the app will contain only the ‘Comparison’ tab. In this case, the user should provide the UMAP coordinates in the metadata dataframe.
  • Enable live filtering of the marker genes based on all the columns. The filtered table will be used as input for the enrichment analysis.

Fixes

  • Fix the case in write_object when the gene variance filtering leaves the chunk with one or zero genes.
  • Stop allowing the user to calculate the ECC or perform the merging to a list with less than two partitions by raising an exception.
  • Sort the k values numerically in the merge_resolutions function.
  • Fix the qualpalr colour space parameter in the add_metadata function.
